RoomType.rationale: RoomType.Monster. The sim represents room-type membership by pool bucket rather than a per-encounter attribute: `sts2_rl/rooms.py`'s `_underdocks_rooms()` places `"living_fog"` in `normal_keys`, which `seam/rooms_and_map` (the picker) and `rewards.GOLD_REWARD_RANGES` (keyed by `RoomType.MONSTER`, see the gold-ladder guard) both key off. EXECUTED: `grep -n '"living_fog"' sts2_rl/rooms.py` -- present exactly once, in `normal_keys`.

HasScene.rationale: LivingFogNormal.cs:16: `HasScene => true`. Presentation surface; waived per the monster tier's established precedent.

Slots.rationale: LivingFogNormal.cs:18: `Slots = [bomb1, bomb2, bomb3, bomb4, bomb5, livingFog]` (6 named slots) -- consumed by `CombatState.SortEnemiesBySlotName`/`EncounterModel.GetNextSlot` whenever a creature is added with a non-null SlotName. The sim's `LIVING_FOG_NORMAL = Encounter(id="living_fog_normal", monster_classes=[LivingFog])` passes NO `slots=` -- `encounter.slots` is the empty-tuple default, diverging from the C#'s real 6-element row. This is inert by construction rather than by luck: `living_fog.py`'s own `_bloat` (which spawns a Gas Bomb) and `_slot_index` completely bypass `self.slots`/`sort_enemies_by_slot_name` -- they track occupancy via a custom `GasBomb.slot` int (0..4) and compute the insertion INDEX directly (`CreatureCmd.add(ctx.hooks, bomb, index=idx)`, no `slot_name=` argument, so `sort_enemies_by_slot_name` is never even called), reproducing the same effective ordering SortEnemiesBySlotName would produce given the real 6-slot row (bombs occupy slots 0-4, ahead of the Living Fog's own slot 5, matching the C#'s livingFog-is-last placement). `test_underdocks.py::TestLivingFog`'s slot-order test (`[type(e).__name__ for e in cs.enemies] == ["GasBomb", "LivingFog"]`, then `["GasBomb", "GasBomb", "LivingFog"]` for a second Bloat) pins exactly this and passes (`py -m pytest test/test_underdocks.py -k LivingFog -q`, re-run this batch, 6 passed). A documented, verified reimplementation rather than a gap -- but flagged because the `Encounter.slots` field itself is silently wrong for this unit, which the next reader who trusts that field directly (rather than living_fog.py's own bypass) would get wrong.

AllPossibleMonsters.rationale: The sim has no `Encounter.all_possible_monsters` field; the purpose this member serves (every monster class the encounter can ever field, including summons, for the obs vocabulary / bestiary-style previews) is served by `sts2_rl/vocab.json`'s `monsters` list, which every monster class the roster registers is checked into regardless of whether it starts on the field. EXECUTED: `py -c "import json; m=json.load(open('sts2_rl/vocab.json'))['monsters']; print([c for c in ['LivingFog', 'GasBomb'] if c not in m])"` -> `[]` (all present).

ExtraAssetPaths.rationale: LivingFogNormal.cs:26: preloads the Smog affliction's overlay VFX path. Presentation/asset-preload surface only; waived per the monster tier's established precedent.

GetCameraScaling.rationale: LivingFogNormal.cs:28-31: returns 0.9f, a combat-camera zoom factor. Presentation surface; waived.

GenerateMonsters.maps_to: Encounter(monster_classes=[LivingFog]).create_monsters (base Encounter, monsters/base.py); GasBomb spawns are LivingFog._bloat, not GenerateMonsters
GenerateMonsters.rationale: C# LivingFogNormal.cs:33-36 returns a SINGLE-element list, `(LivingFog.ToMutable(), "livingFog")` -- zero RNG draws. Sim `LIVING_FOG_NORMAL = Encounter(monster_classes=[LivingFog])` (living_fog.py:145-148): one instance, zero draws -- roster/order/draw-count match. The initial creature's slot label ("livingFog") is dropped on the sim side (`monster_slots` defaults to `()`), the SAME shape as the Slots guard above and inert for the identical reason (`_slot_index()`, living_fog.py, returns the hardcoded constant `_BOMB_SLOTS` for a `LivingFog` instance by TYPE dispatch, never reading `creature.slot_name`) -- not filed separately from the Slots guard, same mechanism.

ShouldReceiveCombatHooks.maps_to: n/a -- Encounter has no hook-listener interface
ShouldReceiveCombatHooks.rationale: `EncounterModel.ShouldReceiveCombatHooks => false` (EncounterModel.cs:39), not overridden by this unit. The sim's `Encounter` (monsters/base.py) is a plain dataclass with no `on_*`/hook-listener interface at all -- it is never registered with `HookSystem` (grep `hooks.register` across sts2_rl/: only `Creature.__init__`/`Monster.__init__` call it) -- so it architecturally cannot receive a combat hook, matching the false default by construction rather than by an explicit flag. Faithful.

guards.what: Gold reward ladder (MinGoldReward/MaxGoldReward, inherited from EncounterModel -- not overridden by this unit)
guards.rationale: EncounterModel.cs:64-100: RoomType.Monster -> 10-20, Elite -> 35-45, Boss -> 100-100 (both bounds equal), times AscensionHelper.PovertyAscensionGoldMultiplier under Poverty. sts2_rl/rewards.py:170-174's `GOLD_REWARD_RANGES` pins the identical non-ascension triple `{MONSTER: (10, 20), ELITE: (35, 45), BOSS: (100, 100)}`; rewards.py's own module docstring (line 32) states ascension/Poverty scaling is out of scope, matching this audit's own scope line (`PROMPT.md` Scope section: 'Ascension values: out of scope'). This unit passes no `min_gold`/`max_gold` override to its sim `Encounter`, so `generate_combat_rewards` (rewards.py:885-887) falls through to the room-type default range -- matching the C#'s own inheritance of the base ladder.

guards.what: Per-encounter Rng independence (EncounterModel.cs:41-49's own doc comment: the encounter's Rng is independent of the run's centralized Rng, safe because its state need not survive past the encounter)
guards.rationale: Stream IDENTITY (which Rng object, how it is seeded) is `seam/rng_streams`'s mechanism, not this record's -- cited, not re-verdicted, per PROMPT.md rule 3 and this batch's brief. What IS this record's to check: does the sim's draw actually land on that independent per-encounter Rng rather than a shared/run-level one? `sts2_rl/run.py:1702-1706`'s `create_combat` builds `encounter_selection_rng` via `make_encounter_rng(seed, total_floor, encounter.entry)` (rng.py, verdicted faithful by seam/rng_streams step 21) UNCONDITIONALLY now, on every path: `rng_set.seed` when parity mode is active (string-seeded runs, the conformance/replay path), `self._legacy_encounter_seed` otherwise (run.py:1704-1705) -- threaded into `CombatState`/`Encounter.create_monsters` as `selection_rng` (combat.py:240-243). REVISED from the prior pass: this record used to note that legacy/RL-training runs (`rng_set is None`) fell back to the shared `random.Random`, breaking the game's independence guarantee in that mode. That is no longer true -- `run.py:1694-1701`'s own comment now frames the shared-stream fallback as the PRIOR behavior ('before that it took create_monsters' selection_rng=None arm ... which the game's own isolation guarantee forbids'), and `create_combat` computes an independent per-encounter Rng regardless of `rng_set`. `grep -n rng_set sts2_rl/run_env.py` still returns zero hits (RL training sets no `rng_set`), but it no longer matters: the encounter-selection stream is independent on both paths now. No live or dormant gap here; if anything the prior caveat is moot.
